correctness.rationale: For all n>=2 and 0<=k<=n, a marked set of k nonincident adjacent matching edges is noncrossing and deletion is a bijection to a residual uniform matching, proving the mixed binomial identity. Cycle matching counts give the coefficient. Binomial inversion establishes the entire joint law. Exact crossing mean/variance plus the first two marked moments yield covariance and correlation. For fixed k, residual-size normalized crossing counts satisfy the known CLT, while weights w_n,k<=2/k! and tend to 1/k!, so dominated convergence proves the independent joint limit. A 385-assertion exact finite verifier passed; finite enumeration is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Both total crossing complexity and number of simple isolated chords are canonical statistics of a uniform random chord diagram. The all-n polynomial transform yields an entire natural joint distribution from classical crossing enumerators, not an artificial slice or mere numerical refinement. It exposes an exact negative correlation -sqrt(5/(n+3)) and joint Gaussian–Poisson independence despite finite dependence, offering a clear structural distinction between local isolated components and global crossing fluctuations.
